query: Refractory high-entropy alloys are promising structural materials, but achieving a strong combination of strength and plasticity remains important. What single intervention could improve this strength–plasticity combination? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its expected mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate reference alloy, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Al2O3 ceramic particles to TaNbVTi-based refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) will improve their strength-plasticity combination by introducing TiO precipitates and promoting solid solution strengthening.
generation.conditions: Spark plasma sintering at 1700 °C with a heating rate of 100 °C/min and a constant pressure of 30 MPa
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of TiO precipitates and Al atoms dissolving into the matrix
generation.mechanism: Precipitation strengthening and solid solution strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved compressive yield strength and specific yield strength with a slight sacrifice in plasticity
generation.boundary: The addition of Al2O3 ceramic particles should not exceed 15 vol.% to avoid significant degradation of plasticity
generation.uncertainty: The optimal volume fraction of Al2O3 addition for achieving the best strength-plasticity combination is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare TaNbVTi-based RHEAs with varying volume fractions of Al2O3 addition (0%, 5%, 10%, 15%) and test their compressive properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Al2O3 ceramic particles does not result in improved compressive yield strength and specific yield strength, or if the plasticity is significantly degraded, the hypothesis is falsified

In this work, a series of lightweight TaNbVTi-based RHEAs were fabricated by mechanical alloying (MA) followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructural evolution and its effects on mechanical properties were analyzed.
## 2. Experimental Procedures
The TaNbVTi-based RHEAs were prepared by powder metallurgy (P/M) method. High purity (>99.5 wt.%) Ta, Nb, V, Ti elemental powders in equiatomic composition were mixed with Al2O3 powders as the raw materials, and then blended with a planetary ball-millers for 6 h at 120 rpm under argon atmosphere at a temperature of 25 °C. The average particle size of Ta, Nb, V, Ti and Al2O3 powders is 24.5 μm, 26.1 μm, 22.6 μm, 29.1 μm and 0.3 μm, respectively. Figure 6b presents fracture strain dependence of compressive specific yield strength of the TaNbVTi-based RHEAs compared with other previously reported typical RHEAs [,]. Surprisingly, the results highlight the extraordinary mechanical properties of the TaNbTiV based RHEAs compared with many other previously reported RHEAs with moderate plasticity. These exceptional mechanical features suggest a promising method for enhancing RHEAs through the addition of ceramic reinforcements.
